navigation_rules.q: Two power-driven vessels are crossing. The vessel that has the other on her starboard side shall:
choices: A. Stand on and maintain course
B. Give way and avoid crossing ahead
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 15: crossing situation — the vessel with the other on her starboard side shall keep out of the way.

navigation_rules.q: A vessel not under command shall display which day signal?
choices: A. Two black balls in a vertical line
B. Three black balls in a vertical line
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 27: two all-round red lights and two black balls in a vertical line.

navigation_rules.q: A vessel engaged in fishing (trawling) displays which lights at night?
choices: C. White over green over white
D. Red over green over white
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 26: trawling vessels display red over white all-round lights in addition to sidelights.

navigation_rules.q: In a head-on situation between two power-driven vessels, each shall alter course to:
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 14: each shall alter her course to starboard to pass port-to-port.

navigation_rules.q: What does 'underway' mean under COLREGs?
choices: A. Not at anchor, aground, or made fast to shore
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 3: 'underway' means not at anchor, aground, or made fast to the shore. A vessel drifting with engines stopped is still underway.

navigation_rules.q: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre shall display:
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 27: ball-diamond-ball day signal, red-white-red lights at night.

navigation_rules.q: What sound signal does a power-driven vessel make when intending to overtake another on her starboard side?
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 34: two short blasts = 'I intend to overtake you on your port side' (vessel being overtaken is on starboard).

navigation_rules.q: What is the minimum number of crew required on the bridge for a safe navigational watch under STCW?
navigation_rules.ref: STCW Chapter VIII: the OOW may be the sole lookout in daylight with clear visibility, but a lookout must be posted at night or in restricted visibility.

navigation_rules.q: Two power-driven vessels are meeting head-on on reciprocal courses. Which action complies with COLREGs Rule 14?
choices: A. Both alter course to starboard and pass port-to-port
B. The give-way vessel alters to port
D. The vessel with the other on her port side gives way
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 14 (head-on): each vessel shall alter course to starboard so as to pass on the port side of the other.

navigation_rules.q: A power-driven vessel overtaking another in a narrow channel intends to overtake on the overtaken vessel's starboard side. What whistle signal is required by Rule 34?
choices: A. Two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts
B. Two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 34(c)(i): 'I intend to overtake you on your starboard side' = two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts.

navigation_rules.q: A vessel constrained by her draught may display which additional day signal in a narrow channel?
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 28: a vessel constrained by her draught may display a black cylinder where it can best be seen.

navigation_rules.q: Which vessel is defined as 'not under command' under COLREGs Rule 3?
choices: B. A vessel which through some exceptional circumstance is unable to manoeuvre and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel
C. A vessel drifting with engines stopped
D. A vessel restricted by her draught
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 3(g): 'vessel not under command' means a vessel which through some exceptional circumstance is unable to manoeuvre as required by these Rules.

navigation_rules.q: A sailing vessel and a power-driven vessel are crossing. Under Rule 18, who gives way?
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 18(a): a power-driven vessel underway shall keep out of the way of a sailing vessel.

navigation_rules.q: A vessel engaged in fishing (other than trawling) with gear extending more than 150 m horizontally shows which day signal?
choices: A. A black cone apex upward in the direction of the gear
B. A black cone apex downward
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 26(c)(iii): when gear extends more than 150 m horizontally, a black cone apex upward in the direction of the gear.

navigation_rules.q: What is the significance of five short and rapid blasts sounded by a power-driven vessel?
choices: B. Doubt or danger of the other vessel's intentions/actions
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 34(d): five short and rapid blasts = doubt/danger signal when vessels in sight of one another.

navigation_rules.q: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre performing an operation (e.g., cable-laying) that restricts her to starboard-side passage shows which lights at night?
choices: A. Red-white-red all-round plus the restricted-manoeuvre lights
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 27(d): a vessel restricted in ability to manoeuvre performing an operation restricting passage to one side shows red-white-red all-round lights plus the side to keep clear of.

navigation_rules.q: Under Rule 19 (restricted visibility), a vessel detecting another vessel by radar alone must avoid altering course to:
choices: A. Port for a vessel forward of the beam (other than crossing)
B. Starboard for a vessel abeam
C. Either side for a vessel abaft the beam
D. Starboard for a vessel forward of the beam
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 19(d)(i): avoid altering course to port for a vessel forward of the beam, other than a crossing vessel.

navigation_rules.q: A vessel aground shows which anchor lights/shapes in addition to those of a vessel at anchor?
choices: A. Two all-round red lights (night) / three black balls (day)
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 30(d): a vessel aground shall show two all-round red lights and three black balls (day), plus anchor lights/shapes.

navigation_rules.q: Which statement about a 'vessel constrained by her draught' versus 'vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre' is correct?
choices: B. Draught-constrained shows a cylinder; RAM shows ball-diamond-ball
D. Draught-constrained shows balls; RAM shows a cone
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 28 (cylinder for draught-constrained) vs Rule 27 (ball-diamond-ball for RAM).

navigation_rules.q: An air-cushion vessel (hovercraft) operating in the non-displacement mode shows, in addition to sidelights, which all-round light?
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 23(c): air-cushion vessels in non-displacement mode shall exhibit an all-round flashing yellow light.

navigation_rules.q: A WIG (wing-in-ground) craft, when taking off/landing/in flight near the surface, keeps clear of which vessels?
choices: D. Only vessels not under command
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 18(f): a WIG craft, when taking off, landing and in flight near the surface, shall keep well clear of all other vessels.

navigation_rules.q: Under Rule 9 (narrow channels), a vessel of less than 20 m or a sailing vessel shall:
choices: A. Impede the passage of a vessel which can safely navigate only within a narrow channel
B. Not impede the passage of such a vessel
C. Anchor in the channel centre
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 9(c): a vessel of less than 20 m or a sailing vessel shall not impede the passage of a vessel that can safely navigate only within a narrow channel.

navigation_rules.q: Vessels fishing in close vicinity of other fishing vessels have special signal requirements. Two vessels fishing on the same side (pair trawling) show:
choices: A. One white light over one red light each
B. Their fishing lights plus a searchlight directed at the other vessel
D. A flashing yellow light each
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 26(c)(ii)/Annex II: when shooting/hauling or gear obstructs, extra signals; vessels fishing in close vicinity show searchlight or signals per Annex II.

navigation_rules.q: Which sentence best states the Rule 2 caveat (responsibility)?
choices: A. Nothing in the Rules exonerates from neglect of any precaution required by ordinary practice of seamen or special circumstances
B. The Rules may be ignored in emergencies
C. The Master may delegate compliance
D. Local rules override COLREGs entirely
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 2(a): nothing exonerates neglect of precautions required by the ordinary practice of seamen or by the special circumstances of the case.

navigation_rules.q: A pilot vessel on pilotage duty shows which lights when at anchor?
choices: B. Pilot lights (white over red) plus anchor lights
D. Blue flashing light plus anchor lights
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 29(b): a pilot vessel when not engaged on pilotage duty shall show the lights for a similar vessel of her length; when at anchor she shows anchor lights in addition to pilot lights (Rule 29 + Rule 30).

navigation_rules.q: A vessel towing alongside (pushing ahead, rigid connection) shows which lights?
choices: A. The lights of a power-driven vessel (side, stern, masthead as applicable)
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 24(a): a power-driven vessel when pushing ahead or towing alongside (except a rigid connection in a composite unit) shows the ordinary power-driven vessel lights; a rigid composite unit shows the lights of a power-driven vessel.

navigation_rules.q: What additional signal may a vessel at anchor in a fairway alert other vessels to her position?
choices: A. Rapid ringing of the bell for 5 seconds, plus three strokes if over 100 m
C. One prolonged blast every 2 minutes
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Annex II/Rule 35(g): a vessel at anchor may sound rapid bell ringing for about 5 seconds every minute; over 100 m, also gong aft, plus one preceded/tollowed by one stroke.

navigation_rules.q: Under Rule 10 (Traffic Separation Schemes), a vessel may enter a TSS for which reason?
choices: B. Crossing the scheme, joining/leaving at its ends, or in cases of immediate danger
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 10: vessels shall use TSS lanes as designated; crossing at as near as practicable to right angles to the general direction of traffic flow.

navigation_rules.q: A dredger working in a fairway with an obstruction on her port side shows which light on that side?
choices: A. Two all-round red lights on the obstructed side
B. Two all-round green lights on the passable side
C. A single all-round white light
navigation_rules.ref: COLREGs Rule 27(d): vessels RAM performing dredging/underwater operations show two all-round red lights on the obstructed side and two all-round green lights on the side vessels may pass.

navigation_rules.q: Which of the following is required by STCW Chapter VIII before taking over the navigational watch?
choices: A. The relieving officer must confirm the ship's position, course, speed, and have adjusted to night vision
B. Only a signature in the deck log
C. The Master's verbal approval alone
D. Testing the main engine at full power
navigation_rules.ref: STCW Code Chapter VIII/4: the relieving officer shall satisfy himself of the ship's estimated/charted position, course, speed, and that vision is adjusted to prevailing light conditions before taking over the watch.

solas_marpol.q: SOLAS Chapter II-2 deals with:
choices: B. Fire protection, fire detection and fire extinction
solas_marpol.ref: SOLAS Chapter II-2 covers fire protection, fire detection, and fire extinction.

solas_marpol.q: MARPOL Annex V regulates:
solas_marpol.ref: MARPOL Annex V: prevention of pollution by garbage from ships.

solas_marpol.q: What is the minimum freeboard determined by?
solas_marpol.ref: The International Load Line Convention determines minimum freeboard based on ship type, season, and zone.

solas_marpol.q: MARPOL Annex VI addresses:
solas_marpol.ref: MARPOL Annex VI: prevention of air pollution from ships (SOx, NOx, particulate matter).

solas_marpol.q: Under SOLAS, how often must lifeboats be launched during drills?
solas_marpol.ref: SOLAS III/19.3.1: lifeboats must be launched with their assigned crew every 3 months.

solas_marpol.q: What is the purpose of the ISM Code?
solas_marpol.ref: International Safety Management (ISM) Code requires a Safety Management System (SMS) with documented procedures and audits.

solas_marpol.q: MARPOL Annex VI SOx emission limit in Emission Control Areas (ECAs) is:
solas_marpol.ref: MARPOL Annex VI: 0.5% sulphur content limit globally, 0.1% in ECAs (effective 2020).

solas_marpol.q: What does the term 'load line' refer to?
choices: B. Maximum legal draft to which a ship may be loaded
solas_marpol.ref: Load Line Convention: marks on the ship's hull indicating the maximum legal draft in different water conditions.

solas_marpol.q: Under MARPOL Annex VI, what is the maximum sulphur content (mass) permitted for fuel oil used onboard ships outside Emission Control Areas (ECAs) since 1 January 2020?
solas_marpol.ref: MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 14.1.3: sulphur content of fuel oil used onboard shall not exceed 0.50% m/m outside ECAs (from 1 March 2020 carriage ban on non-compliant fuel).

solas_marpol.q: Within an Emission Control Area (ECA), the maximum fuel sulphur content is:
solas_marpol.ref: MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 14.4: sulphur content within ECAs shall not exceed 0.10% m/m.

solas_marpol.q: Under MARPOL Annex I, discharge of oily bilge water from machinery spaces is permitted only if the oil content of the effluent without dilution does not exceed:
solas_marpol.ref: MARPOL Annex I Reg. 15.3: oily bilge water discharge permitted when oil content < 15 ppm with operating oil-filtering equipment and outside special areas conditions.

solas_marpol.q: Which annex of MARPOL governs the prevention of pollution by sewage from ships?
solas_marpol.ref: MARPOL Annex IV: Prevention of pollution by sewage from ships.

solas_marpol.q: Under SOLAS Chapter V, from what date must all ships carry an Electronic Chart Display and Information System (ECDIS) per the performance standards (for ships built after 1 July 2012 on keels after that date on new builds)?
choices: A. ECDIS is voluntary on all ships
B. Phased mandatory carriage per SOLAS V/19.2.10 implementation schedule
solas_marpol.ref: SOLAS V/19.2.10 as amended (MSC.317(88)): phased ECDIS mandatory carriage schedule by ship type and size.

solas_marpol.q: The ship's Oil Record Book Part I (machinery space operations) must be retained onboard for at least:
solas_marpol.ref: MARPOL Annex I Reg. 17: Oil Record Book entries shall be preserved onboard for a period of three years after the last entry.

solas_marpol.q: Under SOLAS Regulation III/19, abandon ship drills and fire drills must be conducted (for passenger ships) at intervals of:
solas_marpol.ref: SOLAS III/19.2.1.2: on passenger ships, abandon ship and fire drills shall take place weekly.

solas_marpol.q: The ISM Code requires the company to establish a Safety Management System (SMS). Which document is the company's written statement of its safety objectives and commitment?
choices: B. The Safety and Environmental Protection Policy
C. The Master's Overriding Authority letter
solas_marpol.ref: ISM Code Para 2: the company should establish a safety and environmental protection policy; para 4 defines the SMS which includes it.

solas_marpol.q: Under MARPOL Annex V (garbage), which of the following may be discharged into the sea outside special areas?
choices: B. Food comminuted to <25 mm at ≥3 nm from nearest land
solas_marpol.ref: MARPOL Annex V Reg. 4/6: food waste comminuted/ground to <25 mm may be discharged ≥3 nm from nearest land (outside special areas); plastics prohibited everywhere.

solas_marpol.q: Under SOLAS Regulation II-2, the Fire Control Plan must be permanently exhibited and show, among other items:
choices: A. Location of fire pumps, extinguishers, controls, and ventilation shut-offs
solas_marpol.ref: SOLAS II-2/15.2.3: fire control plans shall show fire-control stations, fire pumps, extinguishers, dampers, fire detectors, and access routes.

solas_marpol.q: The Ship Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP) is required under:
solas_marpol.ref: MARPOL Annex I Reg. 37: every oil tanker of 150 GT and every ship other than an oil tanker of 400 GT and above shall carry a SOPEP approved by the Administration.

solas_marpol.q: Ballast Water Management under the BWM Convention requires D-2 performance standard discharge of viable organisms below specified limits. The D-2 standard applies to ballast water exchange/operations how?
choices: A. Replaces D-1 exchange entirely since 2017
B. As a performance standard applied via type-approved BWMS after the phase-in schedule
solas_marpol.ref: BWM Convention (2004, in force 8 Sep 2017) Reg. D-2: ships shall discharge ballast water that meets D-2 organism concentration limits via type-approved Ballast Water Management Systems per the phase-in.

ntm_interpretation.q: An NTM states: 'Light buoy FL(3)10s at 03°02'N 101°20'E reported UNLIT.' What should mariners do?
choices: A. Ignore — it will be fixed soon
B. Navigate with caution, do not rely on it at night, report the discrepancy
ntm_interpretation.ref: Standard NTM practice: treat unlit aids as unreliable, use alternative navigation, report to the hydrographic office.

ntm_interpretation.q: An NTM announces: 'Drilling rig to be positioned at 05°30'N 100°30'E, radius 500m, surface to seabed.' What is the safe distance?
ntm_interpretation.ref: The exclusion zone is 500m radius from the stated position — vessels must stay outside this area.

ntm_interpretation.q: An NTM states: 'Dredging operations in the fairway. Depths reduced to 8.5m. Dredger 'MUD WARRIOR' standing by on VHF Ch 12.' What should a vessel with 9m draft do?
choices: B. Transit with caution maintaining at least 1m underkeel clearance, contact the dredger on VHF Ch 12
ntm_interpretation.ref: With 8.5m depth and 9m draft, the vessel would be aground. Cannot transit safely. Must use alternative route or wait for dredging to deepen the channel. (Answer: C — avoid the area entirely is most correct as 9m draft > 8.5m depth)

ntm_interpretation.q: A 'dredged depth maintained at 10m below chart datum' means:
choices: A. The water is always exactly 10m deep
B. Minimum depth of 10m is guaranteed at lowest astronomical tide (LAT)
ntm_interpretation.ref: Charted depths are referenced to chart datum (typically LAT). Dredging maintains this minimum depth.

ntm_interpretation.q: An NTM cancels a previous notice (NTM 25(T)/2023). What does the mariner do?
choices: A. Assume the hazard is resolved
B. Remove NTM 25(T)/2023 from the list of active temporary notices
ntm_interpretation.ref: Cancellation means the temporary notice is no longer in force — the hazard should be resolved or the information superseded.

ntm_interpretation.q: A Temporary & Preliminary Notice to Mariners (T&P NM) differs from a Permanent NM in that:
choices: A. It is published only weekly
B. Its information is of a temporary nature or subject to change, and is not immediately incorporated into permanent charts
C. It applies only to naval vessels
D. It does not require chart correction
ntm_interpretation.ref: T&P NMs convey information that is temporary (dredging, buoy changes pending) or preliminary (permanent change expected); they are consolidated in the T&P list and not cut into charts until made permanent.

ntm_interpretation.q: A Notice to Mariners states: 'Buoy No. 3 in position 03°00'.2N, 101°18'.5E is UNLIT until further notice.' The primary navigational action for the mariner is:
choices: A. Ignore the buoy since it is unlit
B. Treat the buoy as unlit and pass with caution, annotating the chart and planning alternate fixing
C. Report the buoy as wrecked
D. Shift to the next lane only
ntm_interpretation.ref: UNLIT marks mean the aid's light is unreliable: the mariner must annotate the chart, adjust the passage plan for reduced aid availability, and maintain extra vigilance/alternate position fixing.

ntm_interpretation.q: The Annual Summary of Admiralty Notices to Mariners is used primarily to:
choices: B. Provide consolidated T&P NM status and other annual information (e.g., maritime radio services, amended blocks)
C. List new chart editions only
ntm_interpretation.ref: The Annual Summary (NP247(1)/(2)) consolidates currently valid T&P NMs and contains annual notices on maritime radio, weather services, etc.

ntm_interpretation.q: Chart correction by NM cut-and-paste requires the mariner to:
choices: A. Paste the correction block over the old information and record the NM number/year in the chart's corner
C. File the NM and ignore the chart until a new edition
D. Correct only the largest-scale chart
ntm_interpretation.ref: Standard chart correction practice: apply the NM block to the affected chart(s), note the NM number/year beside the correction, and maintain the chart correction log.

ntm_interpretation.q: An NTM announces that a light's character changed from Fl(2) R 10s to Fl R 5s. The mariner must correct:
choices: B. The chart(s), the List of Lights entry, and update any route/plan annotations referencing the old character
C. Nothing — lights are corrected by the manufacturer
D. Only the tidal stream atlas
ntm_interpretation.ref: Light character changes require chart amendment plus correction of the List of Lights (ALL volumes affected) and review of passage plans referencing the light.

ntm_interpretation.q: A 'Preliminary Notice to Mariners' (P) announces an upcoming permanent change. Its function is to:
choices: A. Substitute for chart correction permanently
B. Alert mariners early so they can plan, pending the new chart edition/publication
ntm_interpretation.ref: (P) NMs give early warning of changes to be incorporated in forthcoming chart editions, allowing pre-emptive planning before blocks are issued.

ntm_interpretation.q: An NTM references 'depths are in metres and fathoms'. Under this chart's units statement, the soundings are:
choices: B. Mixed: metres for depths under 21 and fathoms+feet in deeper waters (typical older charts)
ntm_interpretation.ref: Charts annotated 'depths in metres and fathoms' use metres for shallow soundings and fathoms/feet for deeper soundings — the units statement governs interpretation; modern charts use metres only.

ntm_interpretation.q: A JLM (Marine Department Malaysia) NTM announces a traffic diversion in the Malacca Strait TSS due to a drilling operation. Under COLREGs Rule 10, vessels should:
choices: A. Ignore the diversion if outside territorial waters
B. Comply with the announced routing measures as IMO-adopted scheme amendments, cross at right angles if crossing
C. Anchor in the traffic lane
D. Fish in the precautionary area
ntm_interpretation.ref: TSS amendments announced through NTMs reflect IMO-adopted routing; Rule 10 requires compliance with traffic flow and right-angle crossing.

ntm_interpretation.q: The term 'Wreck — uncharted, reported' on a radio navigational warning means:
choices: A. The wreck is surveyed and charted
B. A wreck reported but not yet surveyed; position may be approximate and danger may be greater than shown
D. The wreck is marked by a lightvessel
ntm_interpretation.ref: 'Reported' wrecks have unverified positions from third-party reports; mariners must give wide clearance until surveyed and charted.

ntm_interpretation.q: Radio Navigational Warnings (Navtex/NAVAREA) and printed NTMs are complementary because:
choices: A. They duplicate each other entirely
B. Navtex provides immediate broadcast of urgent warnings; printed NTMs provide the permanent/consolidated record for chart correction
D. NTMs are only for fishermen
ntm_interpretation.ref: Urgent warnings are broadcast (NAVTEX/NAVAREA/Inmarsat EGC); the printed NM system provides the auditable, consolidated correction record — both are required components of chart maintenance.

ntm_interpretation.q: An NTM correction block includes a small circle with the words 'Wk 27m'. On the chart this annotation represents:
choices: A. A waypoint 27 nautical miles away
B. A wreck with 27 metres depth of water over it
C. A wharf of 27 m length
D. A water tower 27 m high
ntm_interpretation.ref: Chart abbreviation 'Wk' = wreck; a number beside a wreck symbol denotes the depth of water over the wreck (e.g., Wk 27m = 27 m clearance).

ntm_interpretation.q: The NM 'Dredging operations in position ... from 070001Z to 150001Z MAR' — what does the 'Z' suffix denote?
ntm_interpretation.ref: The 'Z' suffix denotes Zulu time (UTC), standard in all NMs and radio warnings to avoid time-zone ambiguity.

ntm_interpretation.q: A chart correction is to be applied to two charts. The NM block is drawn for the small-scale chart only. The mariner should:
choices: B. Construct an equivalent correction on the larger-scale chart by hand, consistent with the NM's information
C. Request a paper block from the publisher only
D. Wait for the next edition
ntm_interpretation.ref: When an NM block applies to one chart only, corrections on other affected charts are made by hand from the NM's textual information, keeping scales and positions consistent.

ntm_interpretation.q: The 'Notices to Mariners' published by the Marine Department Malaysia (Jabatan Laut Malaysia) are primarily concerned with:
choices: B. Malaysian waters: port notices, buoyage, dredging, obstructions, and navigation restrictions in Malaysian jurisdictions
ntm_interpretation.ref: JLM NTMs announce Malaysian-local navigation information — port circulars, buoy changes, restrictions, dredging — complementing ADMIRALTY NMs for Malaysian waters.

ntm_interpretation.q: If two NTMs conflict (one announces a buoy's relocation, a later one cancels it), which applies?
choices: B. The later NM in date order; later information supersedes earlier, and the chart correction log must reflect the sequence
D. The one with the larger chart number
ntm_interpretation.ref: NTMs are applied in strict date order; a later NM cancelling an earlier one supersedes it, and the correction log records the supersession.

port_operations.q: In Port Klang, what does VTS stand for and what is its primary function?
choices: A. Vessel Traffic Service — monitors and coordinates ship movements
B. Verified Technical Standard — inspection protocol
C. Very Tidal System — tidal monitoring
D. Vessel Transit Speed — speed limit system
port_operations.ref: Vessel Traffic Service provides monitoring, advisory, and organizational services to ensure safe navigation in the port approach.

port_operations.q: What is the purpose of a Ship Security Plan (SSP) under ISPS Code?
choices: B. Security procedures for threat levels 1-3
port_operations.ref: ISPS Code requires SSP documenting security measures at Security Level 1 (normal), Level 2 (heightened), Level 3 (exceptional).

port_operations.q: What is a Port State Control (PSC) inspection?
choices: A. Flag state inspection at home port
B. Inspection by a foreign port to verify compliance with international conventions
port_operations.ref: PSC: coastal states inspect foreign vessels to verify compliance with SOLAS, MARPOL, STCW, Load Line.

port_operations.q: What are the three components of the Ship Security Certification process?
choices: B. Ship Security Plan, Ship Security Officer, Company Security Officer
port_operations.ref: ISPS: Ship Security Plan (SSP), Ship Security Officer (SSO), and Company Security Officer (CSO) form the security framework.

port_operations.q: What is pilotage?
choices: B. The act of a licensed pilot navigating the vessel in port waters
port_operations.ref: Pilotage: a licensed maritime pilot with local knowledge boards and navigates the vessel through port waters and channels.

port_operations.q: Port Klang comprises three terminals. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
port_operations.ref: Port Klang's terminals: Northport (Malaysia), Westports, and Southpoint (cruise/small craft). Tanjung Pelepas (PTP) is a separate port in Johor.

port_operations.q: The Port Klang Authority (PKA) is established under which legislation?
choices: A. Port Authorities Act 1963 (Act 171 / Port Klang Authority Act)
port_operations.ref: Port Klang Authority was established under the Port Authorities Act 1963 (now Port Klang Authority Act), as the statutory port regulator and landlord.

port_operations.q: A vessel departing Port Klang must notify the VTS (Klang Vessel Traffic Service) at what point per standard reporting procedures?
choices: A. Sailing report/departure report at departure and position reports at designated reporting points
C. Only in case of emergency
D. Only when carrying dangerous goods
port_operations.ref: Klang VTS standard reporting: sailing (departure) report upon leaving berth, plus position reports at designated waypoints within the VTS area.

port_operations.q: Under the ISPS Code, a Port Facility Security Assessment (PFSA) is conducted by:
choices: A. The port facility itself without oversight
B. The Recognized Security Organization (RSO) on behalf of the Designated Authority
port_operations.ref: ISPS Code Part A/15: PFSA is carried out by the port facility's personnel, the RSO, or the Designating Authority; approved by the D.A.

port_operations.q: Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) activation in Port Klang waters triggers a response from:
choices: B. The designated flag state authority and, within port limits, the port facility security officer and relevant Malaysian authorities (MMEA/Marine Dept)
C. No one — it is a silent alarm
port_operations.ref: SSAS alerts route to flag administration and company; within port waters, local authorities (Marine Dept/MMEA/port facility) coordinate the response under ISPS Part B guidance.

port_operations.q: Port State Control (PSC) inspections in Malaysian ports are conducted under which regional MOU?
port_operations.ref: Malaysia is a member authority of the Tokyo MOU on Port State Control in the Asia-Pacific Region.

port_operations.q: A PSC officer detains a vessel due to a defective lifeboat davit. The detention is recorded in the Tokyo MOU database (APCIS). To release the vessel, the operator must:
choices: B. Rectify the deficiency to the PSC authority's satisfaction and obtain a follow-up inspection clearing the detention
port_operations.ref: Tokyo MOU procedure: detention is lifted after rectification verified by re-inspection; the deficiency and clearance are recorded in APCIS.

port_operations.q: Which document proves a ship's compliance with the ISM Code and is held by the company (not the ship)?
port_operations.ref: ISM Code: the DOC is issued to the company after verifying SMS ashore; the SMC is issued to each ship after verifying onboard implementation.

port_operations.q: Pilotage in Port Klang for vessels above a specified gross tonnage is:
choices: B. Compulsory within the port limits (per Port Authority regulations), except exempted vessels
port_operations.ref: Port Klang Authority regulations make pilotage compulsory for specified vessel sizes within port limits, with exemptions for certain coastal/short-strait vessels.

port_operations.q: A container vessel berths at Westports with a defective crane on the quay. Which authority coordinates the safety exclusion zone around the defective crane?
choices: A. The terminal operator (port facility) with PKA oversight
port_operations.ref: Port facility safety management (ISPS Part A/16) and port authority oversight (PKA as regulator) coordinate such zones; the terminal operator manages day-to-day ops.

port_operations.q: Under Port Klang VTS, a 'precautionary area' is defined as:
choices: A. An area where anchoring is encouraged
B. An area within a TSS/VTS where vessels must navigate with particular caution and report
port_operations.ref: Precautionary areas (per IMO routing and VTS practice) require heightened vigilance, reporting, and careful navigation due to converging traffic or hazards.

port_operations.q: Dangerous goods arriving at Port Klang by sea require which documentation under the IMDG Code?
choices: A. Dangerous Goods Declaration (DGD) with proper shipping name, class, UN number, and packing group
D. A verbal notice to the pilot
port_operations.ref: IMDG Code Ch. 5.4: Dangerous Goods Declaration with proper shipping name, UN number, class, packing group, EMS, and other mandatory fields.

port_operations.q: A ship at anchorage in the Port Klang Outer Anchorage must maintain:
choices: A. A proper anchor watch per SOLAS V/34-1 and the SMS procedures, monitoring position and traffic
B. No watch if the anchor holds
D. Watch only during PSC inspections
port_operations.ref: SOLAS V/34-1 (Master's responsibility) and SMS watchkeeping arrangements require a safe anchor watch monitoring position, dragging risk, and traffic.

port_operations.q: The 'Port Clearance' required before a vessel sails from Port Klang is issued by:
choices: A. The shipping agent after clearance from Customs, Immigration, Port Health, and the Port Authority
port_operations.ref: Port clearance is granted after all port formalities (Customs, Immigration, Quarantine/Port Health, Authority dues) are completed, typically coordinated by the agent.

port_operations.q: Under Port Klang regulations, a vessel shifting between terminals within the port limits generally requires:
choices: A. A new pilotage engagement and VTS notification for the shift
port_operations.ref: Inter-terminal shifts within port limits remain subject to pilotage and VTS reporting requirements per port regulations.

port_operations.q: Under PKA Notice KS/LPK/01/2025, what is the maximum trim limit 'by astern' for a vessel with LOA less than 200 metres navigating within Port Klang limits?
port_operations.ref: PKA Notice KS/LPK/01/2025: vessels LOA <200m — maximum trim 2.5 m 'by astern'.

port_operations.q: Under PKA Notice KS/LPK/01/2025, a vessel with LOA exceeding 200 metres has a maximum trim 'by astern' of:
port_operations.ref: PKA Notice KS/LPK/01/2025 para 1(ii): LOA >200 m — maximum trim 4.0 m 'by astern'.

port_operations.q: Under PKA Notice KS/LPK/01/2025, when a vessel's trim exceeds the specified limits in an emergency, who must the shipping agent submit a written request to?
port_operations.ref: PKA Notice KS/LPK/01/2025 para 2: written request to LPK (Port Klang Authority); approval subject to specified conditions.

port_operations.q: According to the Port Klang DG Transshipment Guideline, which IMO Class is NOT permitted for transshipment at all (with one exception)?
choices: D. IMO Class 3 Flammable Liquids (PG III)
port_operations.ref: Port Klang DG Transshipment Guideline item 1(i): IMO Class 1 Explosives not permitted except 1.4S.

port_operations.q: Under the Port Klang DG Transshipment Guideline, are Infectious Substances (IMO Class 6.2) permitted for transshipment?
choices: B. No — Class 6.2 Infectious Substances are on the not-permitted list
port_operations.ref: Port Klang DG Transshipment Guideline item 1(xiii): IMO Class 6.2 Infectious Substances not permitted for transshipment.

port_operations.q: Per the Port Klang DG Transshipment Guideline, dangerous goods on the restricted list (except Class 1) may still be considered for transshipment on a case-by-case basis. What must the shipper do?
choices: B. Make an advance inquiry to the Authority providing UN No., IMO Class, and other details, subject to additional safety precautions imposed
port_operations.ref: Port Klang DG Transshipment Guideline item 2: case-by-case consideration subject to additional safety/security precautions; advance inquiry with UN No. and IMO Class details advisable.

port_operations.q: Per PKA Notice KS/LPK/10/2015, which IMDG Code amendment did Port Klang adopt effective 1 January 2016?
port_operations.ref: PKA Notice KS/LPK/10/2015 para 1: LPK adopted all 37-14 IMDG Code amendments effective 1 January 2016.

port_operations.q: Per PKA Notice KS/LPK/10/2015, what must the importer/manufacturer provide to LPK before discharging vehicles/equipment meeting SP961 requirements (UN 3166/3171)?
port_operations.ref: PKA Notice KS/LPK/10/2015 para 6: Letter of Indemnity (LOI) submitted to LPK before discharge (import) or loading (export) for SP961-compliant vehicles/equipment.

port_operations.q: Per PKA Notice KS/LPK/10/2015, who must make the dangerous goods declaration for UN 3166/3171 vehicles for import, transhipment and transit cargo?
choices: A. The shipping agent (ejen perkapalan); the forwarding agent for export
port_operations.ref: PKA Notice KS/LPK/10/2015 para 3: DG declaration by shipping agent (import/transhipment/transit) and forwarding agent (export).

port_operations.q: Per the Port Klang Marine Handbook, what is the general speed limit for all vessels within Port Klang waters?
port_operations.ref: Port Klang Marine Handbook §1.8: all vessels shall navigate at a safe speed and in no case exceed 12 knots.

port_operations.q: Per the Port Klang Marine Handbook, what is the speed limit for vessels navigating within 300 metres of wharves or mooring structures?
port_operations.ref: Port Klang Marine Handbook §1.8: within 300 m of wharves/mooring structures — not exceeding 8 knots.

port_operations.q: Per the Port Klang Marine Handbook, the minimum under-keel clearance (UKC) for a vessel with LOA exceeding 200 metres and/or draft exceeding 10 metres in Port Klang waters is:
port_operations.ref: Port Klang Marine Handbook §1.7: UKC minimum 1.5 m for vessels LOA >200 m and/or draft >10 m; 1.0 m for smaller vessels.

port_operations.q: Per the Port Klang Marine Handbook, is pilotage compulsory in Port Klang?
choices: B. Compulsory — Port Klang is declared a Compulsory Pilotage District
D. Only for vessels over 100,000 GT
port_operations.ref: Port Klang Marine Handbook §2.1: 'Port Klang is declared a Compulsory Pilotage District' — all vessels entering, leaving, or navigating within limits must engage a licensed pilot.

port_operations.q: Per the Port Klang Marine Handbook, where is the Quarantine Anchorage position located?
choices: A. Deep Water Point South between Latitudes 03°02.0'N and 03°03.0'N
port_operations.ref: Port Klang Marine Handbook §1.4: Quarantine Anchorage at Deep Water Point South between 03°02.0'N and 03°03.0'N.

port_operations.q: Per the Port Klang Navigation Safety Guidelines, which VHF channel is used for communications between ships and pilots in the pilotage district?
port_operations.ref: Port Klang Nav Safety Guidelines §1(iii): VHF Ch12 for all communications between ships and pilots; pilots maintain Ch12 listening watch at all times.

port_operations.q: Per the Port Klang Navigation Safety Guidelines, in the South Channel, when two vessels meeting both exceed which criteria does the inbound vessel wait at the Pilot Boarding Ground?
choices: A. Length exceeding 260 m or draft exceeding 12 m
port_operations.ref: Port Klang Nav Safety Guidelines §2(i) South Channel: inbound waits at PBG when meeting a vessel of length >260 m or draft >12 m.

port_operations.q: Per the Port Klang Navigation Safety Guidelines, in the North Channel, which vessel has unimpeded passage when both inbound and outbound vessels exceed 150 m LOA?
choices: D. The vessel bound for Westport
port_operations.ref: Port Klang Nav Safety Guidelines §2(ii) North Channel: when both inbound and outbound exceed 150 m LOA, the outbound vessel has unimpeded passage.

port_operations.q: Per the Port Klang Navigation Safety Guidelines, when two vessels bound for different terminals arrive simultaneously at the Pilot Boarding Ground, which proceeds first?
choices: A. The vessel bound for Northport (ahead of Westport)
B. The vessel bound for Westport (ahead of Northport)
port_operations.ref: Port Klang Nav Safety Guidelines §2(iv): the vessel bound for Northport proceeds ahead of the Westport-bound vessel to embark the pilot.

port_operations.q: The Port Klang 'Fallback Procedures for Systems Breakdown' are designed to maintain which function when primary systems fail?
choices: B. Essential port operations (VTS, communications, EDI, gate systems) through manual/alternative procedures
port_operations.ref: PKA Fallback Procedures: maintain essential operations — VTS, communications, EDI/document exchange, gate operations — via alternative/manual procedures during systems breakdown.

emergency_procedures.q: In GMDSS, what is the frequency for Digital Selective Calling (DSC) distress alerts on VHF?
emergency_procedures.ref: GMDSS VHF DSC distress alerts are transmitted on Channel 70 (156.525 MHz). Voice follow-up on Channel 16.

emergency_procedures.q: What is the first action when a person falls overboard?
choices: B. Throw a lifebuoy, sound alarm, mark position with MOB button, assign a lookout
emergency_procedures.ref: Standard MOB procedure: throw lifebuoy, sound the alarm, mark GPS position, assign lookout, manoeuvre using Williamson turn.

emergency_procedures.q: What does EPIRB stand for and what is its function?
choices: A. Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon — transmits distress position to satellites
B. Emergency Propulsion and Idle Rescue Boat
C. Electronic Pilot Information Radio Beacon
D. Emergency Platform Inflatable Rescue Boat
emergency_procedures.ref: EPIRB: 406 MHz beacon that transmits vessel identity and position to COSPAS-SARSAT satellites for search and rescue.

emergency_procedures.q: What is the primary fire-fighting medium for machinery space fires?
choices: C. Fixed CO2 or total flooding gas system
emergency_procedures.ref: Fixed CO2 or clean agent total flooding systems are primary for engine room fires; water is secondary due to electrical hazards.

emergency_procedures.q: What does 'MAYDAY' signify in radio communication?
choices: B. Distress — imminent danger to life or vessel
emergency_procedures.ref: MAYDAY = distress (grave and imminent danger, immediate assistance required). PAN-PAN = urgency. SÉCURITÉ = safety.

emergency_procedures.q: A DSC distress alert on VHF Channel 70 is acknowledged by a coast station. The vessel should then shift to which channel for subsequent distress traffic?
emergency_procedures.ref: ITU Radio Regulations / GMDSS: VHF DSC distress alerts are sent on Ch 70; subsequent distress traffic moves to Ch 16.

emergency_procedures.q: The 406 MHz EPIRB transmits its distress signal to:
choices: B. COSPAS-SARSAT satellites for position determination and routing to RCC
C. The nearest port authority directly
emergency_procedures.ref: COSPAS-SARSAT 406 MHz EPIRBs are satellite-detected; the system computes position (with GPS if GNSS-equipped) and routes alerts to Mission Control Centres and RCCs.

emergency_procedures.q: The SART (Search and Rescue Radar Transponder), when interrogated by a 3-cm (X-band) radar, displays on the rescuer's screen as:
choices: A. A series of 12 equally spaced dots extending outward from the SART's position
emergency_procedures.ref: SART responds to X-band radar with 12 blips in a radial line (approx 8 nm range); the first blip marks the SART position; only 3-cm radar triggers it.

emergency_procedures.q: In a 'Man Overboard' situation under the Williamson Turn, the helm order sequence is:
choices: A. Hard over to the side of the casualty, then hard over opposite when 60 degrees from original course
D. Maintain course and launch lifeboat
emergency_procedures.ref: Williamson Turn: put rudder hard over toward the casualty's side; after deviating 60° from original course, reverse to hard over the opposite way; brings the vessel on reciprocal course near the MOB position.

emergency_procedures.q: Total flooding of a machinery space with CO2 requires, before release:
choices: A. Verification that the space is evacuated, alarms sounded, ventilation stopped, dampers closed, and engines stopped
B. Only the Chief Engineer's presence
emergency_procedures.ref: SOLAS II-2/Ch. FSS Code Ch. 5 and SMS procedures: pre-release checks include evacuation confirmation, alarm, ventilation/dampers closed, machinery stopped, and a timed delay before release.

emergency_procedures.q: A fire in the accommodation is being fought with a water hose while an adjacent space contains electrical panels. Before directing water near the panels, the attack team must:
choices: A. Isolate electrical power to the affected panels to prevent electrocution
D. Open all doors for ventilation
emergency_procedures.ref: Standard fire-fighting safety: de-energize electrical equipment before applying water; CO2/dry powder preferred on live electrical fires.

emergency_procedures.q: The 'MAYDAY' spoken distress call may only be used when:
choices: A. A vessel or person is in grave and imminent danger and requires immediate assistance
B. There is any doubt about position
emergency_procedures.ref: ITU Radio Regulations Art. 44 / GMDSS: MAYDAY signals indicate grave and imminent danger requiring immediate assistance; priority over all other traffic.

emergency_procedures.q: A 'PAN PAN' urgency call differs from MAYDAY in that it denotes:
choices: A. A very urgent message concerning the safety of a ship or person, but no grave and imminent danger
emergency_procedures.ref: ITU RR Art. 44: URGENCY signal PAN PAN (x3) for urgent safety messages not constituting distress; SAFETY signal SÉCURITÉ for navigational/meteorological warnings.

emergency_procedures.q: Under SOLAS III/29, a lifeboat's launching arrangements must be such that the boat can be launched:
choices: A. Within 5 minutes of the abandon ship signal with the ship underway making 5 knots in calm water
emergency_procedures.ref: SOLAS III/29.2.3 + LSA Code 4.4.7: launch within 5 min of the signal; for tankers of certain sizes, launching at 5 knots ahead speed is required.

emergency_procedures.q: The immersion suit's primary function in an abandon-ship scenario is:
choices: A. To provide thermal protection and buoyancy, reducing cold-water immersion risk
emergency_procedures.ref: LSA Code 4.3: immersion suits provide inherent buoyancy and thermal insulation; donning within 2 minutes; protection against cold water.

emergency_procedures.q: Under the IMDG Code EmS Guide, which extinguishing medium is strictly contraindicated on a fire involving Class 4.3 dangerous goods (substances which in contact with water emit flammable gases)?
emergency_procedures.ref: IMDG Code EmS Guide: Class 4.3 reacts dangerously with water to produce flammable or explosive gases. Water must never be applied directly to the cargo; smother with dry agent or inert gas.

emergency_procedures.q: The On-Scene Coordinator (OSC) for a multi-ship SAR operation is normally designated by:
choices: A. The Rescue Coordination Centre (RCC) or by agreement among the vessels
emergency_procedures.ref: IAMSAR Manual Vol. II: the SMC (at the RCC) designates the OSC, or the OSC may be agreed by consensus among vessels on scene.

emergency_procedures.q: During a fire drill, a scenario requires boundary cooling of an adjacent compartment containing cargo. Boundary cooling is achieved by:
choices: A. Continuously spraying water on the bulkhead/deck adjacent to the fire to prevent heat spread/ignition
emergency_procedures.ref: Standard boundary cooling practice: continuous water spray on adjacent boundaries to prevent heat transfer and auto-ignition of neighbouring cargo/spaces.

emergency_procedures.q: Following a collision, the immediate priority sequence under standard damage-control doctrine is:
choices: A. Preserve life → contain/limit damage (stability, flooding) → then property
B. Save cargo → notify owners → then crew
C. Check engines → then crew → then hull
emergency_procedures.ref: Damage control doctrine (SOLAS II-1/SMS): life safety first; then damage stabilization (flooding/fire); then property/environment — consistent with ISM emergency preparedness.

emergency_procedures.q: A crew member falls overboard at night. Besides the Williamson Turn and MOB mark on GPS, the immediate first actions include:
choices: A. Sounding the alarm, throwing a lifebuoy with light/smoke float, posting extra lookouts, and illuminating with searchlight
B. Stopping engines immediately and drifting
D. Sending a PAN PAN only
emergency_procedures.ref: Standard MOB procedure: alarm; lifebuoy with light/smoke marker; extra lookout; searchlight illumination; keep casualty in sight; report to Master; then the chosen turn (Williamson/Andersen/Scharnow per ship's SMS).

maritime_malay.q: Apakah maksud 'Kawasan Perairan Sekatan' dalam notis pelayaran?
choices: B. Kawasan dilarang masuk tanpa kebenaran
maritime_malay.ref: 'Kawasan Perairan Sekatan' = restricted waters — vessels prohibited from entering without authorization.

choices: A. Alat untuk memasak di kapal
B. Alat bantuan navigasi seperti pelampung, rumah api, dan beacon
maritime_malay.ref: AtoN (Aids to Navigation): pelampung (buoys), rumah api (lighthouses), beacon — membantu pelayaran selamat.

maritime_malay.q: Apakah maksud 'Kedalaman Air' (Charted Depth) pada carta?
choices: B. Kedalaman minimum di bawah datum carta (biasanya LAT)
maritime_malay.ref: Kedalaman carta diukur dari datum carta (biasanya Lowest Astronomical Tide) — minimum depth guaranteed.

choices: A. Jarak dari permukaan laut ke dek
B. Jarak dari lunas kapal ke dasar laut
maritime_malay.ref: Underkeel clearance = jarak menegak antara titik terendah lunas kapal dengan dasar laut.

maritime_malay.q: Apakah bahasa yang digunakan dalam Notis Pelayar (NTM) di Malaysia?
choices: C. Dwibahasa (Bahasa Melayu dan Bahasa Inggeris)
maritime_malay.ref: NTM Malaysia diterbitkan dalam dwibahasa — tajuk dan maklumat penting dalam kedua-dua bahasa.

maritime_malay.q: Apakah maksud 'Laluan Kapal' pada peta pelayaran (chart)?
choices: B. Traffic lane — lorong laluan khusus dalam Traffic Separation Scheme
maritime_malay.ref: 'Laluan Kapal' merujuk traffic lane dalam TSS — koridor pergerakan satu arah yang ditetapkan IMO.

choices: B. Vessel Traffic Service — perkhidmatan memantau dan mengatur pergerakan kapal serta memberi maklumat keselamatan
maritime_malay.ref: VTS = Vessel Traffic Service: perkhidmatan interaksi dengan trafik kapal untuk memantau, mengatur, dan menasihati keselamatan pelayaran.

choices: A. Struktur tepi laut untuk berlabuh dan memunggah muatan
maritime_malay.ref: 'Wharf/quay' = struktur bersambung ke darat sepanjang tepi air, kapal berlabuh di sebelahnya untuk memunggah/memuat.

maritime_malay.q: Dalam notis pelayaran JLM, frasa 'kapal dilarang berlabuh' menunjukkan kawasan tersebut ialah:
choices: B. No anchoring area — kawasan larangan berlabuh (biasanya kerana kabel dasar laut atau paip)
maritime_malay.ref: 'Dilarang berlabuh' = no anchoring — biasanya kerana kabel komunikasi/paip bawah dasar laut yang boleh rosak oleh anchor.

maritime_malay.q: Apakah 'Kawalan Mula Pelayaran' yang dikeluarkan sebelum kapal bertolak dari pelabuhan?
choices: A. Port clearance — kebenaran rasmi bertolak selepas semua formaliti selesai
maritime_malay.ref: Port clearance dikeluarkan selepas Kastam, Imigresen, Kesihatan, dan Pihak Berkuasa Pelabuhan menyelesaikan formaliti — kebenaran bertolak.

choices: B. Pasang tertinggi dan surut terendah berlaku semasa bulan purnama/bulan baru — julat pasang surut terbesar
maritime_malay.ref: Spring tide: julat pasang surut terbesar, berlaku selepas bulan purnama/bulan baru apabila tarikan matahari-bulan sejajar.

maritime_malay.q: Apakah maksud 'Sempadan Perairan' dalam konteks notis pelayaran?
choices: B. Maritime boundary — sempadan perairan wilayah/negara yang menentukan bidang kuasa
maritime_malay.ref: 'Sempadan Perairan' = maritime boundary sempadan bidang kuasa perairan wilayah/negara.

maritime_malay.q: Frasa 'Dilaporkan oleh kapal lain' (reported by another vessel) dalam NTM menunjukkan maklumat tersebut:
choices: A. Telah disahkan oleh Jabatan Laut
B. Belum disahkan — kedudukan mungkin tidak tepat dan bahaya mungkin lebih besar
D. Adalah untuk kapal perang sahaja
maritime_malay.ref: 'Reported' (unverified) information — kedudukan tidak disahkan oleh tinjauan rasmi; mariner perlu beri clearances lebih luas.

maritime_malay.q: Apakah maksud 'Kedalaman Carta 21m' di bawah garisan dasar laut yang ditanda?
choices: B. Kedalaman minimum diukur dari datum carta (biasanya LAT) di titik tersebut
maritime_malay.ref: Soundings diukur dari datum carta (Lowest Astronomical Tide) — 21m ialah kedalaman yang dijamin pada datum tersebut.

choices: B. Kapal yang membantu menggerakkan/memanuver kapal besar dalam pelabuhan
maritime_malay.ref: Tugboat: kapal khusus untuk menunda/mendorong kapal besar semasa manuver pelabuhan, dock, dan laluan sempit.

maritime_malay.q: Frasa 'Berhati-hati — Kerja Penorekan' (dredging operations) dalam NTM bermaksud:
choices: B. Kerja pengerukan dasar laut — kapal perlu laluan jauh dari kapal kerja dan risiko
maritime_malay.ref: Dredging = pengerukan dasar laut (biasanya untuk memperdalamkan laluan); kapal kerja menunjukkan isyarat RAM dan mariner perlu laluan selamat.

maritime_malay.q: Apakah 'Lampu Isyarat Bahaya' pada boya menunjukkan?
choices: A. Bahaya di kawasan sekitar boya — kapal perlu elak dan rujuk carta/notis
maritime_malay.ref: Boya bahaya (isophase/occulting light pada isolated danger mark) menandakan bahaya setempat — kapal perlu beri jarak selamat.

maritime_malay.q: Dalam Bahasa Malaysia, 'Ketua Pegawai Keselamatan Kapal' merujuk kepada:
choices: A. Ship Security Officer (SSO) di bawah kod ISPS
maritime_malay.ref: SSO (Ship Security Officer) bertanggungjawab atas pelaksanaan dan penyelenggaraan Pelan Keselamatan Kapal di bawah kod ISPS.

choices: B. Berlabuh di kawasan yang ditetapkan khas untuk kapal berlabuh selamat
C. Berlabuh di tengah laluan kapal
maritime_malay.ref: Anchorage = kawasan yang ditetapkan dalam carta/notis untuk kapal berlabuh — selamat dari laluan kapal, dalam air, dan dengan dasar sesuai.
